Not every animation is "play this when that happens". Two stable tools cover the rest.

## Motion values are signals

[`moveValue`](/docs/reference/move-value-function) holds a number, [`moveTransform`](/docs/reference/move-transform) maps it onto any output range, and [`moveSpringValue`](/docs/reference/move-spring-value) smooths a value with spring physics. They are plain signals, so they compose with `computed` and work under zoneless change detection.

:::code meter.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-meter',
  template: `
    <input type="range" min="0" max="100" aria-label="Progress" (input)="set($event)" />
    <div [style.transform]="transform()">●</div>
  `,
})
export class Meter {
  /** The driver: any `Signal<number>` works; `moveValue` is a writable one. */
  protected readonly progress = moveValue(0);

  /** Map the driver onto whatever the UI needs. */
  protected readonly x = moveTransform(this.progress, [0, 100], [0, 260]);

  /** Let a spring smooth a value instead of following it rigidly. */
  protected readonly springX = moveSpringValue(this.x, { stiffness: 170, damping: 18 });

  protected readonly transform = computed(() => `translateX(${this.springX()}px)`);

  protected set(event: Event): void {
    this.progress.set(Number((event.target as HTMLInputElement).value));
  }
}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/signals.ts#L5-L27)

::playground[signals]

Drag the progress control: the position is derived directly from the signal, and the spring follows it. Under reduced motion the spring jumps straight to its target. [`moveSpringValue`](/docs/reference/move-spring-value) creates an effect, so call it from an injection context (a field initialiser or constructor) or pass `injector` explicitly.

## Imperative animation: `MoveAnimator`

When a handler or a service should animate an element it holds a reference to, inject [`MoveAnimator`](/docs/reference/move-animator). It takes an `Element` or an `ElementRef`, handles reduced motion and server rendering for you, and its `finished` promise **always resolves** — unlike raw WAAPI, whose `finished` rejects on cancel.

:::code toast-dismiss.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-toast-dismiss',
  template: `
    <div #toast>Saved</div>
    <button type="button" (click)="dismiss()">Dismiss</button>
  `,
})
export class ToastDismiss {
  readonly #animator = inject(MoveAnimator);
  protected readonly toast = viewChild.required<ElementRef<HTMLElement>>('toast');

  async dismiss(): Promise<void> {
    // `finished` always resolves: natural finish, cancel(), a second play(), or teardown.
    await this.#animator.animate(
      this.toast(),
      { opacity: [1, 0], y: [0, 12] },
      { duration: '180ms' },
    )?.finished;
    this.toast().nativeElement.remove();
  }
}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/signals.ts#L31-L51)

`pseudoElement` animates `::view-transition-new(root)` (or any pseudo-element) through the same API, which is how a View Transition reveal is written. Unsupported browsers get a no-op, and under reduced motion the pseudo-element animation is skipped while your DOM change still applies. See the [imperative playground](/demos/imperative).

## Choosing

- A finite animation on an element you hold a reference to: `MoveAnimator`.
- A continuous number you bind in the template (pointer position, scroll progress, a slider): motion values.

**Related:** [`moveValue` playground](/demos/values) · [`MoveAnimator` playground](/demos/imperative) · [Patterns](/docs/patterns)
